Up to 10 million stone blocks were brought from a mountain 40 km away to build Angkor Wat. 🛶 Watch 28 years of building in 26 seconds. ⏱️

King Suryavarman II started it around 1122: first a moat 190 m wide, then a raised platform of fill. The sandstone came from Mount Kulen, about 40 km away, most likely moved by water on canals and rivers. Laterite inside, sandstone outside: 5 to 10 million blocks, up to 1.5 tons each, rising into five towers shaped like lotus buds, 65 m high.

The twist: nobody knows for sure what binds the blocks. Resin and lime have been suggested, but the glue is still a mystery.

yt_description:
Angkor Wat was commissioned by Suryavarman II and built c. 1122–1150. Kulen sandstone was quarried ~40 km away and likely moved by canal/river; the temple used 5–10 million sandstone blocks (max ~1.5 t), with laterite for hidden structure, on ~3 million m³ of fill. Moat 190 m wide, perimeter >5 km; five towers, the central one 65 m above ground. The binding agent is still unidentified. The world's largest religious structure.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angkor_Wat · https://www.britannica.com/topic/Angkor-Wat
Figures are historical estimates. Stylised 3D animation.
